bandReport.notes: BAND RANGE DIFFERS FROM THE ASSIGNMENT. I was told to expect roughly items 46-65; the pages actually carry items 39-60, contiguous, with no gaps and no repeats. I trusted the pages as instructed. Consequence for the merge: this band OVERLAPS the preceding band on items 39-45 (a duplicate is free) and, more importantly, items 61-65 are NOT on my pages - whoever owns page index 14 must cover them. Per-page layout, read c1 then c2 as instructed: p10 = 39, 40 | 41, 42, 43 (booklet page 21); p11 = 44, 45, 46, 47 | 48, 49, 50 (page 23); p12 = 51, 52 | 53, 54, 55 (page 25); p13 = 56, 57, 58 | 59, 60 (page 27). NOTHING STRADDLES THE GUTTER on any of these four pages - every item's stem, statement list and full option block sit inside a single column - so there was no c1/c2 assembly to get wrong here. Item 39 begins cleanly at the top of p10-c1 with clear blank space above it (item 38 finished on an earlier page), and item 60 ends with all four options plus the '[ P.T.O.' rule at the foot of p13-c2, so neither band edge cuts an item. COLUMN CROPS: clean on all four pages; _render.json reports gutterFound true for page indices 10-13. The crops overlap slightly at the gutter, and the only visible artefact of that is cosmetic - the printed page number in the footer sits astride the split, so it appears in full at the right edge of c1 and its last digit re-appears at the left edge of c2 (p10 '21' / '1', p11 '23' / '3', p12 '25' / '5', p13 '27' / '7'). No question text is affected and no crop is sliced mid-line. SCAN QUALITY: this is a bilingual booklet and the Hindi setting on the reverse of each leaf shows through as faint ghost text across both columns on every page. It is legible enough to be distinguished from the English foreground and did not obstruct any reading. VERBATIM ODDITIES, transcribed as printed and NOT corrected: (1) item 53's stem is awkwardly worded in the original - 'of the following four rivers, three of them pour into one of them which joins the Indus direct' and then 'which one is such river that joins the Indus direct' - both 'joins the Indus direct' (not 'directly') and the missing article in 'is such river' are the booklet's own; (2) item 50 asks 'Which of the above statements is/are correct?' where the neighbouring two-statement items (42, 58) ask 'Which of the statements given above is/are correct?' - the difference is printed, not mine; (3) item 57 prints the word 'least' in bold italic for emphasis ('which one is the least water-efficient crop') - transcribed as plain text since the field carries no formatting; (4) item 41 asks about 'the history of ancient India' while two of the three named figures are conventionally placed later - printed as is. ASCII-SAFE TRANSCRIPTION, following the convention of the 2025 bands: the booklet's curly quotation marks are transcribed as straight ASCII quotes (item 44 'Songs from Prison', item 52 'palm oil', item 56 'Rare earth minerals', item 59 'Climate-Smart Village', and the double-quoted passage that opens item 60), and item 45's option strings are printed with EM DASHES between the three administrative units (Paragana - Sarkar - Suba) which I have transcribed as plain ASCII hyphens; the reading is unambiguous in every case. Genuine mid-word hyphens were kept as printed ('Climate-Smart', 'semi-arid', 'Semi-Arid', 'water-efficient', 'Montagu-Chelmsford', 'Pandu-lena'). Two line-wrap hyphens were joined into whole words: item 51 statement 1 'pre-dominant' -> 'predominant'; item 40 has none. NO ITEM WAS UNREADABLE and no item number skips. No question in this band contains mathematics or a data grid, so there is no LaTeX and no pipe table. CLASSIFICATION NOTES for the two items whose catalog home is genuinely arguable: item 50 (International Mother Language Day / Bangla in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan) is filed under Current Affairs and IR because the testable hook of statement 1 is which UN agency made the declaration, though its statement 2 is squarely historical; item 51 (permaculture vs conventional chemical farming) is filed under Geography / Agriculture and Soil Geography with subtopic 'Irrigation and Land Use', which is the closest listed subtopic but not a comfortable fit - a subtopic along the lines of 'Sustainable Farming Practices' would suit it better and the catalog may be worth extending. Item 56 (seabed licences, rare earth minerals on the seafloor) is likewise a borderline Geography / Current Affairs item, filed under Economic Geography and Natural Resources / Mineral Resources.
